cohort: The study utilized responses from 34,222 mothers who delivered live births in the five years preceding the NFHS-5 survey.
finding: The study identified spatial hot spot clustering of CS rates in districts of Sikkim, Tripura, Assam, and Manipur, and found that maternal age (30-49 years), first birth order, highest educational level, high body mass index, and highest wealth quintile were significant determinants of CS, with varying regression coefficients by district.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from the fifth round of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-2021), including mothers who delivered live births in the five years preceding the survey.
